genius-80.preamble: Down solutions must be suitably 14 in order to be 17, not briefly edited, before being inserted in the grid. Three across clues have solutions that are 17 and are not further defined.
genius-80.source: https://fifteensquared.net/2010/02/28/guardian-genius-80-february-2010-puck/ (quotes the preamble; its bracketed glosses left out)

genius-81.preamble: Solutions are divided into four groups of seven. Each member of that group begins with the same letter. The definition in all 28 of these clues is normal (and is placed at the correct clue number), but all subsidiary parts of these clues have been swapped around. The correct subsidiary part for any definition can always be found in another clue where the solution begins with the same letter. All 28 subsidiary parts of these clues ignore the initial letter of the solution. The four letters that begin the solutions may be arranged to give something to drive.

genius-93.preamble: Seven clues require ill-advised exchanges before solutions are entered in the grid. The resulting solutions are non-words. In these seven clues, the definitions (indicated by the letter counts) are pre-operative and the cryptic parts are post-operative. All other clues are normal.
genius-93.source: https://fifteensquared.net/2011/04/03/guardian-genius-93-by-paul/ ("In the preamble we were told that")

genius-99.preamble: Each clue, presented in the form of a 10, contains a definition and a jumble of the letters of the solution. The jumble always starts at the start or ends at the end of a word in the clue. Seven of these jumbles contain one superfluous letter. These lead in clue order to the puzzle's theme.

genius-100.preamble: The spelling of several well-known (but undefined) entries is incorrect, which may not be to your taste!

genius-105.preamble: Seventeen clues lack a definition and lead to a partner in a well-known pairing. The required grid entry, however, is the other partner in the pairing. With these clues the letter count indicates the solution to the clue, not the word to be entered in the grid.

genius-115.preamble: Ten solutions can also be 30, initially. Any secondary definition or wordplay in their clues leads to the solution as it might appear if it were, indeed, 30 of any 26 12 before 22 down 22 across. With one of these cases, where proverbially the solution cannot be 30, a palatable alternative (carrying the smallest possible 26 14) is required.
genius-115.source: https://fifteensquared.net/2013/02/03/guardian-genius-no-115-by-puck/ ("The preamble read as follows"; numerals are clue references)

genius-117.preamble: Seven clues contain anagrams of their definitions for their solutions. Eight more clues have had their definitions removed and added, superfluously, to eight different clues. The remaining seven clues have had their definitions shuffled randomly.

genius-129.preamble: Eleven clues lead to the second part of a thematically related solution, not further defined. However, the letter counts with these clues refer to the first part of each of these solutions, which is to be entered in the grid.

genius-135.preamble: All solutions are thematic, wholly or in part. All clues contain normal definitions but, with 18 of them, the wordplay ignores the thematic element.

azed-2688.preamble: Nine across and nine down clues lead in their definitions to Spoonerisms of the correct answers to be entered. Subsidiary indications in these clues lead to the correct answers themselves. In the remaining clues (except 16) the definitions have been distorted by one Spoonerism per clue. Subsidiary indications in these clues likewise lead to the correct answers. Competitors should submit with their solutions a clue of the latter type to the asterisked definition at 16. NB Spoonerisms may be either consonantal, e.g. WHITEBAIT/BITE (or BIGHT) WAIT, or vocalic, e.g. BUNTING/BIN TONGUE, and may be accompanied by changes in punctuation. Bracketed numbers after clues indicate the length of grid entries throughout.
azed-2688.source: Guardian printable copy uploads.guim.co.uk/2023/12/21/AZ_2688_(24th_Dec).pdf (reader's overprint doubles removed)

azed-2655.preamble: Each clue, except 8, is a passage from which the printer has removed a hidden answer, closing the gap and sometimes taking liberties with the punctuation, but not disturbing the order of the remaining letters. Example: Vaulting above tunnel entrance appears inane, scary. Answer: PESTO. Undevilled version: Vaulting above tunnel entrance appears in an escape story. Every passage, when complete, makes reasonable sense. Competitors should submit with their entries a PD clue to replace the asterisked definition at 8. NB Preference is given to PD clues in which the break before and after the answer omitted (before and after omission) does not occur at the ends or beginnings of words in the clue. Please give the full undevilled version of your clue as well as the clue itself.
azed-2655.source: Guardian printable copy uploads.guim.co.uk/2023/05/06/AZ_2655_(07th_May).pdf (reader's overprint doubles removed)

azed-2595.preamble: Most of the entries contain one or two misprints, producing non-words. Every clue contains a definition of the un-misprinted entry and a subsidiary indication of the form entered. The misprints may be read to form a timely message. Competitors should submit with their entries a normal cryptic clue to the first two words of the message.
azed-2595.source: Guardian printable copy uploads.guim.co.uk/2022/03/05/AZ_2595_(06th_Mar).pdf (the anniversary lunch notice printed beside it left out)

azed-2566.preamble: In a Playfair word square the code phrase (in which no letter recurs) is followed by the remaining letters of the alphabet, I doing double duty for I and J. To encode a word it must first be split into pairs of letters, e.g. CR IT IC AL. Each pair is then to be seen as forming the diagonally opposite corners of a rectangle within the word square, the other two corners being the encoded form. Thus, in the example shown, CR gives SG (not GS, which RC would give). Where a pair of letters appears in the same row or column in the word square, its encoded form is produced from the letter immediately to the right of or below each respectively. For the last letter in a row or column the first letter in the same row or column becomes the encoded form. Thus IC becomes CE. When all the pairs are encoded, the word is joined up again, thus CRITICAL is encoded as SGCICEOP. The answers to the four asterisked clues, which are without definitions, must be encoded in the diagram. The code phrase (of two words, one of them an abbreviation) describes the answers to the asterisked clues. It must be deduced with the help of the answers to normal clues, so that the diagram may be completed.
azed-2566.source: Guardian printable copy uploads.guim.co.uk/2021/08/12/AZ_2566_(15th_Aug)_(1).pdf (read off the page image: the text layer starts mid-passage; the example square ORANG/ESTIC/KBDFH/LMPQU/VWXYZ is a graphic)

nation-3403.source: the puzzle's own 5-down clue states the theme (no preamble printed)
